The instantaneous power at time $t=t_{1}$ 2. Starting from $t=0$, the average power of $F$ over the time interval up to $t_{1}$
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The block has mass m, starts from rest, and is on a smooth horizontal surface, so there is no friction. The constant horizontal force F is the net horizontal force. By Newton's second law, the acceleration is a = F/m. Since the block starts from rest, its velocity at time t1 is v(t1) = a t1 = Ft1/m. The instantaneous power delivered by the force is P = Fv, so at t = t1, P(t1) = F(Ft1/m) = F^2 t1/m. For the average power from 0 to t1, first compute the displacement: s = (1/2) a t1^2 = Ft1^2/(2m). The work done by the force is W = Fs = F^2 t1^2/(2m). Average power is work divided by time, so P_avg = W/t1 = F^2 t1/(2m).

method.method_draft: Use Newtonian kinematics and work over displacement. Read that the block has mass m, starts from rest, is on a smooth horizontal surface, and is acted on by a constant horizontal force F until time t1. Since the surface is smooth, the net horizontal force is F, so a = F/m. Starting from rest, v(t1) = at1 = Ft1/m. Instantaneous power is P = Fv, so P(t1) = F(Ft1/m) = F^2 t1/m. For the average power from 0 to t1, compute the displacement s = (1/2)at1^2 = F t1^2/(2m), the work W = Fs = F^2 t1^2/(2m), and divide by elapsed time t1 to get P_avg = F^2 t1/(2m).

method.method_draft: Use impulse/energy and time-averaging of power. Read that the force F is constant, horizontal, and unopposed by friction on a mass m initially at rest. From impulse-momentum, mv(t)=Ft, so v(t)=Ft/m. Therefore the instantaneous mechanical power supplied by the force is P(t)=Fv(t)=F^2 t/m, giving P(t1)=F^2 t1/m. For the average power, either integrate this linear power function over the interval, P_avg=(1/t1)∫_0^t1 (F^2 t/m) dt = F^2 t1/(2m), or equivalently use ΔK/t1 with K(t1)=mv(t1)^2/2.
method.CoT_raw: The surface is smooth, so the horizontal force F is unopposed by friction. The block starts from rest. Using impulse-momentum from t=0 to time t: Ft = mv(t), so v(t) = Ft/m. The instantaneous power delivered by a force is P(t) = Fv(t), since the force and velocity are in the same horizontal direction. Therefore P(t) = F(Ft/m) = F^2 t/m, and at t = t1 the instantaneous power is F^2 t1/m. For the average power from 0 to t1, average the time-dependent power: P_avg = (1/t1) ∫_0^t1 (F^2 t/m) dt = (1/t1)(F^2/m)(t1^2/2) = F^2 t1/(2m).
